Standard: All verbal warning signals are IAW MIL-STD-1472, Verbal Warning Signals paragraphs, and the annunciation levels are 6 dB above the level of communications audio at all volume settings, but not to exceed 110 dB. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Verify that the verbal warning signals are IAW MIL-STD-1472, Verbal Warning Signals paragraphs.
(2) Verify the audio signal characteristics (e.g., frequency, duration, intensity) of the verbal warning signals are IAW MIL-STD-1472, Verbal Warning Signals paragraphs.
(3) Verify that the verbal warning signals are 6 dB above the level of communications audio at all volume settings. Demonstration.
  (1) Conduct a demonstration to verify the effectiveness of the verbal alerts to include the perception and recognition by the crewmembers of the alerting condition during possible other concurrent audio events and correct discrimination by the crewmembers of alerting signals in representative noise conditions. The demonstration will be conducted in an environment that incorporates all normal operational stressors to which crewmembers will be exposed in the context of a representative flight profile. The demonstration should include cascading failure scenarios. This evaluation should be in a production representative mock-up. Test.
    (1) Ground or Lab test: Record audio of verbal warning signals and voice communications at all combinations of master and channel volume settings. Prior to entering operational test or operations, verify the standard by the following method(s): Test.
    (2) Ground test: Review ground test results to validate the results from analysis, lab testing, and demonstration.
    (3) Flight test: Review flight test results to validate the results from analysis, lab testing, and demonstration.
